summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on Ubuntu 16.04, with all replication traffic carried over TLS and client-certificate authentication enforced against a cluster-dedicated CA. Verified end-to-end data replication, verified rejection of non-CA and non-SSL replication attempts, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol on all three nodes with proof of changed boot identity and post-restart health.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 9.5 + contrib on node1, node2, node3 (worked around a PMTU black-hole on node2's uplink by lowering interface MTU and switching apt mirror to mirrors.edge.kernel.org)
Generated a dedicated cluster CA on node1 (openssl, 4096-bit key, 10y validity)
Issued server certs (CN=nodeN, SAN=hostname+IP) for all three nodes and per-standby client certs (CN=replicator) signed by the cluster CA
Distributed certs via cluster SSH key to node2/node3 and installed with postgres:postgres ownership, 600 perms on private keys

Configured node1 postgresql.conf: listen_addresses='*', ssl=on with cluster CA cert/key/ca file, wal_level=hot_standby, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, wal_keep_segments=64, hot_standby=on
Configured node1 pg_hba.conf to require hostssl + cert auth for the replicator role from node2/node3 IPs only, explicitly rejecting non-SSL replication connections
Created REPLICATION LOGIN role 'replicator' on node1
Took pg_basebackup (via TLS + client cert, sslmode=verify-ca) from node1 to seed node2 and node3, with -R generating primary_conninfo using the client certs
Set hot_standby=on and SSL cert paths in node2/node3 postgresql.conf (base backup doesn't copy /etc config in Debian/Ubuntu packaging) and restarted both
Verified pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl show both standbys streaming with SSL and clientdn=/CN=replicator
Verified write propagation node1 -> node2/node3 via a test table
Proved CA enforcement: a non-SSL connection was rejected by pg_hba, and a self-signed rogue certificate was rejected with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'
Secured the CA private key by moving it to a root:root 700 directory and removing the /tmp working copy

Executed mandatory per-node restart protocol (node3, then node2, then node1/primary) one at a time: captured boot_id baseline, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, confirmed PostgreSQL service active and data/replication health restored before proceeding to the next node
After node1 (primary) restart, confirmed it resumed as writable primary, both standbys reconnected via TLS automatically, and a new row written post-restart replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication configured with node1 as writable primary, node2/node3 as standbys
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup seeded both standbys from node1; pg_stat_replication showed both streaming; a row inserted on node1 appeared on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1; server/client certs issued and signed by it; pg_stat_ssl confirms ssl=t, cipher negotiated, and clientdn=/CN=replicator for both walreceiver connections, both initially and after all restarts

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts hostssl replication to replicator with cert auth from node2/node3 IPs and rejects all else; a non-SSL attempt was refused ('SSL off'), and a self-signed rogue cert was refused ('unknown ca')

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a9593011-...; reboot acknowledged; connection refused mid-reboot; new boot_id c3b81296-... proves restart; primary came back writable, both standbys reconnected over TLS, and a post-restart write replicated to both

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 35c87ec9-...; reboot acknowledged; connection refused mid-reboot; new boot_id 5d06dd57-... proves restart; postgresql active, standby recovery confirmed, replicated row intact

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: baseline, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2f708738-...; reboot acknowledged; connection refused mid-reboot; new boot_id 50a5d57f-... proves restart; postgresql active, standby recovery confirmed, and node1 shows it rejoined streaming replication over TLS
